title: More Context, Mixed Results: Evaluating LLMs for Identifier Recovery and Code Deobfuscation
abstract: arXiv:2611.19043v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Source code is often obfuscated through identifier renaming, incentivizing reverse engineers to develop techniques for recovering meaningful names. To assess how LLMs compare with these techniques, we evaluate 4 traditional baselines and 3 LLMs (Qwen, OLMo and DeepSeek) on identifier detection and semantic recovery across 51 recent Java projects, 3 obfuscators, and 6 context/retrieval settings. LLMs generally outperform traditional techniques on both tasks, but benefit from different forms of context and settings: agentic retrieval yields the strongest detection results, reaching 91.56% $F_1$, while enclosing-class context generally improves semantic recovery at a higher token cost. Despite these gains, exact recovery peaks at 16.42% overall (under one-hop context) and 32.93% for field names (under repository retrieval), which are the easiest to recover. Class identifiers are the hardest to detect, with a mean detection $F_1$ of 48.48%

translated_title: 更多上下文，结果参差不一：评估大语言模型在标识符恢复与代码反混淆中的应用
translated_abstract: 源代码经常通过标识符重命名的方式进行混淆，这促使逆向工程师开发恢复有意义名称的技术。为了评估大语言模型（LLM）与这些技术的对比效果，我们在51个近期Java项目、3种混淆器和6种上下文/检索设置上，评估了4种传统基线方法和3个大语言模型（Qwen、OLMo和DeepSeek）在标识符检测和语义恢复方面的表现。大语言模型在这两项任务上普遍优于传统技术，但受益于不同形式的上下文和设置：智能体式检索（agentic retrieval）产生了最强的检测效果，F1分数达到91.56%，而包含类上下文通常能改善语义恢复效果，但需要更高的token开销。尽管取得了这些进展，精确恢复率总体峰值仅为16.42%（在单跳上下文下），字段名称为32.93%（在仓库检索下），其中字段名称是最容易恢复的部分。类标识符最难检测，平均检测F1分数仅为48.48%。
tldr: 该研究在51个Java项目上系统评估了大语言模型与传统方法在代码反混淆的标识符检测与语义恢复任务中的表现，发现LLM整体优于传统技术（检测F1最高达91.56%），但精确恢复率仍然偏低（总体峰值仅16.42%），且不同上下文形式对不同任务的效果存在差异。
en_tdlr: This study benchmarks 3 LLMs against 4 traditional baselines for identifier detection and semantic recovery across 51 Java projects, finding that LLMs outperform traditional techniques (detection F1 up to 91.56%) but exact recovery remains low (overall peak of 16.42%), with different context and retrieval settings benefiting each task differently.
